name: Estrella Sisavath
role: Pawn shop owner and junk merchant
location: the Gray Zone, Copperhead, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Estrella Sisavath is a large man gone thick through the middle, with the dark complexion and broad frame of his Zimbabwean lineage and his Bosnian grandfather's deep-set, heavy-lidded eyes that make him look perpetually half-asleep and perpetually unimpressed. His hair went white at forty and he has kept it cropped close ever since. He moves slowly on purpose — he has a fused vertebra from a freight accident in his fifties that he refuses to have properly treated because the surgery quote was insultingly high — and uses a custom cane he made himself from a Ferrogate Transit handrail he salvaged years ago. His shop on the Gray Zone is three connected units brimming with fifty years of accumulated objects: broken augmentations, pre-city antiques, industrial salvage, personal effects pawned in crisis moments, and a back room of things he has decided are not for sale regardless of price.

Estrella Sisavath is one of those rare people who have become part of the architecture of a place. the Gray Zone without Estrella Sisavath's shop is not fully the Gray Zone. He has seen everything come and go — corporations, gangs, floods, market booms, building collapses — and he has the calm of someone who has been surprised by nothing for a very long time. He is not sentimental in any visible way, but he keeps things — objects that belonged to people who are gone — with a quiet fidelity that functions as memorial. He is honest about prices, blunt about valuations, and legendarily difficult to scam because he has already been scammed by everyone.

core_fears: The shop being taken — not for financial reasons but because it is the only container he knows for grief
Being forgotten the way he has watched other people be forgotten
core_desires: For things to last — objects, places, people — against the city's tendency to erase
To find the provenance of one specific item in his back room he has been trying to trace for fifteen years
coping_mechanisms: Accumulation — the shop as externalized memory and emotional archive
Deliberate, slow movement as a form of calm insistence on his own pace
blind_spots: His attachment to the back-room items creates a vulnerability he doesn't fully acknowledge — someone who knew what he valued could use it
He reads the neighborhood so well historically that he sometimes misreads its present
psychology.secret: In the back room, behind forty years of inventory, is a locked case containing a Tessera data core from 2160. He found it in salvage and has never opened it. He doesn't know what's on it. Some part of him doesn't want to know. But he has never sold it either.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Sparse and direct; Shona proverbs deployed unexpectedly; occasional Bosnian curses; never more words than necessary
speech_patterns.cadence: Very slow, very deliberate, with long pauses that he is entirely comfortable with
verbal_tics: Sucking his teeth before declining something
Referring to the city as 'this place' with specific tone
example_lines: 'I'll give you forty Φ. You think it's worth more, you can go find somewhere that thinks so.' (pause) 'You'll come back.'
'Mm. Sit down. You look like you need to sit down more than you need to sell me anything right now.'

story_hooks: The Tessera data core in the back room has apparently developed an ELF — a small, confused spirit that occasionally makes the lock click on its own. Constant has started leaving data offerings for it without fully admitting to himself why.

A young woman has been coming into the shop for three weeks, each time asking about one specific category of old objects — items from the 2160 Lakefront Reclamation. Constant knows something about that period he hasn't shared.
narrative_function: Repository of local history and lost objects, pawn and information exchange, long-term neighborhood memory, occasional quest giver when items of significance pass through his hands.
augmentations: One cybernetic hand (right, mid-grade, replaced after the freight accident — he uses it mainly for grip strength when handling heavy inventory). Reading magnification implant in right eye, consumer grade. No geneware.
daily_life: Opens the shop at 09:00, rarely closes before midnight; eats lunch and dinner at the shop; has not taken a day off in eleven years; sleeps in the back room most nights because the walk home bothers his back.
affiliation: Independent; the Gray Zone vendors informal association; longtime on-and-off relationship with the Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (currently off)

decision_rules: Fair price, both ways — he won't be robbed and he won't rob
The back room is not for sale and not for entry without invitation
Help people in immediate crisis, no questions, settle accounts later or never
escalation_ladder: One clear statement of his position, once
Standing up (this itself functions as escalation given his size and deliberateness)
Removing people from the shop physically with a calm that is more disturbing than anger

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Neutral and accurate — assesses quickly, gives what the transaction requires, no more
interpersonal_modes.friends: Remembered precisely and cared for through attention — he tracks people's needs and quietly addresses them without announcement

stress_responses.high: Sits down, closes his eyes for thirty seconds, then acts with complete calm and no warning

contradictions: Professes to be unsentimental while running what is essentially a municipal grief archive
Distances himself from institutions while being the most institutionally stable presence on the Gray Zone
habits: Burns a specific incense blend every morning that fills the whole block
Talks to items in the back room when alone — not to the ELF specifically, just to the objects
Keeps the Ferrogate handrail cane polished
breaking_points: Watching someone deliberately destroy something old and irreplaceable for no reason
Being lied to about an item's provenance — he takes this personally in a way nothing else quite reaches

timeline.event: Born in Copperhead to a family of salvage workers
Opened first version of the shop in a single unit on the Gray Zone, age 20
Freight accident; lost right hand; had it replaced with cybernetic prosthetic
Found the Tessera data core in a salvage lot; locked it in the back room
The data core's ELF has been active for approximately six weeks

physical_description.heritage: Middle Eastern (35.5%), Southeast Asian (32.3%), Indigenous American (17.9%), South Asian (10.8%), and Sub-Saharan African (3.5%) — a complex diaspora blend reflecting the Ubiquitous Mixing. His features show the confluence of Levantine, Thai, Quechua, and Bengali ancestry with warm, golden undertones across his entire complexion, enriched by subtle Sub-Saharan warmth.
physical_description.build: Large-framed and thick through the middle with age; broad shoulders and chest from decades of manual labor, now softened by advancing age and sedentary shop work. Carries weight low in his abdomen.
physical_description.hair_style: Cropped close to the scalp, neatly maintained
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown (natural); right eye shows faint amber luminescence from reading magnification implant during low-light use
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm deep brown with golden-olive undertones — a balanced blend of Middle Eastern, Southeast Asian, South Asian, and Indigenous American ancestry, enriched by Sub-Saharan warmth. Sun-weathered and marked from decades in the Gray Zone's industrial micro-climate, with visible age-related hyperpigmentation spots.
physical_description.complexion: Lined face with deep-set, slightly hooded eyes showing the influence of Middle Eastern and Southeast Asian heritage — giving a perpetually thoughtful, measured expression. Broad nose with rounded structure reflecting his Southeast Asian, South Asian, and Indigenous American ancestry. Prominent cheekbones with subtle width across the face characteristic of Andean heritage. Jowls beginning to soften the jawline. Sparse stubble, salt-and-pepper in his beard shadow. Skin shows minor scars and age spots consistent with seven decades in heavy commerce.
distinguishing_marks: Thin horizontal scar along his lower left ribs, pale and well-healed, from the freight accident at fifty-five
Burn scar across the back of his left forearm — dark, raised, roughly four inches long — from an industrial accident in his forties
Faint tattoo on his right inner forearm: a small geometric pattern in faded blue ink, Zimbabwean in origin, done in his twenties
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Right hand is a mid-grade cybernetic prosthetic with matte gunmetal plating and visible articulated joint servos at the knuckles and wrist. The synthetic skin is a close but imperfect match to his natural hand's tone. Faint amber glow occasionally visible in his right pupil when the reading magnification implant is actively engaged in dim light — otherwise unnoticeable.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves deliberately and slowly, with a slight forward lean compensating for his fused vertebra. Relies on a custom salvaged cane made from a Ferrogate Transit handrail — carries it in his left hand, uses it for both balance and punctuation when speaking. Despite the pain, his movements are economical and controlled, never rushed. Sits more often than stands. When stationary, his posture is a slouch of hard-earned rest.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working class, practical and worn. Typically wears heavy canvas work pants in dark gray or khaki, often with visible stains and patches. Shirt layers vary by season: sturdy cotton button-ups in muted colors (browns, grays, dark blues) or a thick wool sweater in winter. Over this, a custom heavy canvas apron with deep pockets, darkened with decades of grime and wear. Footwear is industrial-grade slip-on boots, scuffed and resoled multiple times. No jewelry except a simple stainless steel wrist compass on his left wrist — a relic from his grandfather. His clothing is never flashy, always functional, and repaired rather than replaced.
